subject: Civil Engineering
title: Project Delivery Methods
description: A micro-lesson that makes Project Delivery Methods usable.

hook.text: Who designs? Who builds? Who takes risk? The delivery method answers all three questions.

buildup.text: Design-bid-build separates design and construction — the owner hires each independently.

discovery.text: Design-build combines both under one contract — faster delivery, single point of responsibility.

twist.text: CM at risk puts the construction manager in charge early — they guarantee a maximum price.

climax.text: Integrated project delivery (IPD) shares risk and reward — all parties succeed or fail together.

punchline.text: How you organize the team determines whether the project succeeds or fails.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of design-build over design-bid-build?
options: It always produces higher quality buildings
One contract covers both design and construction, enabling faster delivery
It eliminates the need for a construction manager

details.summary: Project delivery methods define the contractual relationships between owner, designer, and builder. Common methods include design-bid-build where design is completed before construction bids, design-build where one entity handles both.
details.whyItMatters: The delivery method chosen determines project speed, cost certainty, risk allocation, and the owner's level of control. Choosing the wrong method can doom an otherwise well-planned project.
takeaways: Design-bid-build separates design and construction into sequential phases
Design-build combines both under one contract for faster delivery
CM at risk provides early contractor input while guaranteeing maximum price

faq.question: Which project delivery method is fastest?
faq.answer: Design-build is typically fastest because design and construction overlap. The builder starts site work while design of later phases continues. This can save 15 to 30% of overall schedule compared to design-bid-build.

faq.question: Why do some public agencies still require design-bid-build?
faq.answer: Design-bid-build separates design from construction, enabling competitive bidding on a fully defined scope. This transparency satisfies public procurement laws that require fair competition on equal terms.
